label: LOCAL ENGINEERING DRILL - shared-lease fair-share admission A/B for finding O1. Not HA, not an SLA, not candidate-bound; shared 4-vCPU host, load generator on the same host.
design: supabase/migrations/20261011000500_tenant_inflight_shared_leases.sql + supabase/functions/_shared/tenant-concurrency.ts: one SECURITY DEFINER RPC per request acquires a lease (tenant resolved from the presented key's SHA-256 with the authentication lookup; fair-share rules over live leases in one scope shared by ingest and policy; serialised by a row lock on the scope row; 60 s expiry), one releases it. UNLOGGED tables in schema app, service_role execute only. Defaults unchanged: capacity 10, per-tenant max 7, floor 2, Retry-After 1 s; capacity is now deployment-wide instead of per isolate.

stack.db: supabase/postgres:17.11.0.004 (kit pin), 185 canonical migrations through 20261011000500 applied to a fresh database; auth/storage stubbed as the repository's PostgreSQL fixture tests do, plus auth.users.email_confirmed_at
stack.rest: postgrest/postgrest:v14.17, default pool 10, kit libpq keepalive/tcp_user_timeout parameters
stack.functions: supabase/edge-runtime:v1.77.4@sha256:ad45164b7548bf5820ed7be714789c17ac2865edce79a09cfb4c3756c3d365a8 (kit pin, pulled via mirror.gcr.io), upstream self-hosted main router (150 MB / 60 s per worker), supabase/functions copied in, Ed25519 entitlement and policy signing configured
stack.gateway: node:24.21.0-alpine3.24 stand-in reverse proxy (/functions/v1, /rest/v1), as in the soak
stack.tenants: two pilot-admitted tenants, 50 seats each: quiet 1 key, noisy owner + 9 member keys; published runtime policy each

workload: unchanged from the per-isolate A/B: 11-key knee profile, per key ingest (2-event batch) : policy = 3 : 1, equal per-key rate, noisy = 10x quiet; 90 s per run; timeout 10 s; max_in_flight 400; per rate the order off, on, off, on with 60 s cool-down; edge runtime restarted per run

lease_cost.what: acquire_tenant_inflight_lease + release_tenant_inflight_lease through the stand-in gateway and PostgREST with the service-role key, functions idle, scope separate from the drill's, 2000 pairs per row

quiet_shed_log_lines_on_arm.ab56-on-1: capacity x3 logged (quiet held 3, 5, 5 of total 10)
quiet_shed_log_lines_on_arm.ab52-on-2: capacity x2 logged (quiet held 3, 4), fair_share x2 (quiet held 5 = its share of 10 / 2)

raw_artefacts_note: load-test outputs and container logs were not retained in the repository; their hashes are listed here

result.bound: MISSED in all 4 on-arm runs (quiet error ratio 1.09-1.74% against <= 0.1%; 5-8 quiet 429/503 per run against 0; quiet p95 328-504 ms against <= 241.2 ms)
result.what_changed_vs_per_isolate_v3: the quiet tenant is never charged to the shared unresolved bucket any more (0 unresolved sheds; its leases are charged to its own tenant from the first request of every new worker); quiet p95 fell from 0.63-1.00 s (v3) to 0.33-0.50 s; no off-arm-style collapse on-arm (goodput 46.3-52.4 HTTP 200/s, 0 drops, 0 timeouts); a deployment-wide cap of 10 now holds across workers and both functions (2 s after every on-arm run 0 live leases; lease_expired logged 0-4 times per on-arm run)
result.why_still_missed: every quiet refusal happened while the quiet tenant itself already held 3-5 leases (its own fair share is 5) and the deployment was at capacity 10: at about 5 quiet requests/s that means individual quiet requests were taking roughly 0.6-1 s, i.e. they were stalled, not starved of admission. The edge runtime still retired workers 43-49 times per on-arm run on its CPU-time soft limit; concurrency admission bounds requests in flight, not CPU or worker restarts on a saturated 4-vCPU host. Quiet error ratio was higher than v3 (1.1-1.7% vs 0.65-0.93%) because a deployment-wide capacity of 10 is half of what two per-isolate limiters admitted
result.off_arm: collapsed in all 4 runs (goodput 8.2-17.9 HTTP 200/s, quiet errors 67-84% timeouts/drops); at 52 rps lower than the per-isolate v3 window (52.0/51.9), so host capacity moved again between windows and the off arm now also pays two lease RPCs per request; under collapse lease RPCs themselves failed (limiter_error and release_failed logged, leases reclaimed by expiry)
result.not_tried: lower capacity, lower CPU limits, preemption of leases granted before a tenant became active; not tried so that the bound is not tuned to this host
